notes: Random 30 of 559 extracted claims, each read against its source window.
3 not real forecasts: a reporter relaying polls, a host reading out betting odds, and a 'told you so' recorded the day after the election.

Reading the boldest-calls and worst-misses lists turned up 3 more: a wishful aside about the Buckeyes and Bengals, and one claim the extractor flipped ('0% chance of a not guilty verdict' came back as 'Trump is acquitted'). These and the reporter/odds cases are removed in data/review.json.
Three rounds of 40 random graded matches, checked for the right market and the right side.
Round 1: 36/40. Two side errors came from grouping 'X wins' with 'X does not win' (the normalizer dropped 'not'), and two claims were aired on or after the day the market resolved. Both fixed.

Rounds 2 and 3: 40/40 each. Reading the top lists also caught two side slips (the model used the real-world outcome to pick a side) and one either/or claim matched to a single market; fixed with prompt rules and rerun.
